newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Shell seeks to lead Brazil natgas market.
newsitem.headline: Shell seeks to lead Brazil natgas market.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell has positioned itself to become a leader in Brazil's promising natural gas market by buying a minority stake in Sao Paulo state-owned Comgas, a company official said.
"There is room here in Brazil for growth and we would like to take part (in the sector)," Shell Brasil S.A. president Willen Goebel told reporters.
He said Shell Brasil would seek to become Brazil's second-largest natural gas distributor once the government approves a new law regulating the opening of the country's oil sector.
"If the law permits, Shell will invest," Goebel said.
Shell Brasil paid 74 million reais for 1.7 billion common shares of Comgas, a 19.86 percent voting stake, from the city of Sao Paulo at an auction Wednesday on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange.
Goebel declined to say what other investments Shell plans in the Brazilian gas sector.
Local press reports said the purchase may be annulled as a result of protest by brokerage firm Bozano, Simonsen, which claimed the auctioneer failed to acknowledge its bid during the auction.

Comgas, which is expected to be privatized in October, hopes to increase gas distribution to 8 million metric tons by 2000 from the current 3 million tonnes. The firm accounts for 30 percent of all natural gas sold in Brazil.
The state government decided to privatize Comgas so that private investors can carry out the company plans to invest $300 million a year by 2000 to expand its gas distribution network in the state.
Goebel said Shell could pay for up to 20 percent of total Comgas investments as a result of the acquisition.
